newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna stocks pare losses as Dow opens up.
newsitem.headline: Vienna stocks pare losses as Dow opens up.

text.p: Austria's ATX blue-chip index ended sharply lower on Monday but well above session lows and eyeing Wall Street, as the U.S. market opened higher in the wake of its sharp falls on Friday, dealers said.

The ATX, which fell more than three percent in intra-day trade, ended 32.97 points, or 2.38 percent, lower at 1,349.78. It was helped by a strong performance from VA Stahl -- the sole stock to buck the weak trend.
The steel products group, which has seen its shares come under pressure recently, saw sporadic buying lift its stock 5.5 schillings to 562.

Traders, who see technical support at 1,300, said any upside of the ATX was dependent on the performance of Wall Street, which rocked world equities markets on Friday by clocking up its biggest one-day point loss since October 1997.
"We've seen some consolidation which ought to be over at these levels," said one trader. But he added. "Let's see what the Americans are going to do."
Microchip producer AMS led Austrian decliners, closing 6.04 percent weaker at 1,010.05.
AMS joins oil group OMV, Austria's most heavily-weighted company, and cardboard manufacturer Mayr-Melnhof in releasing half-year results on Thursday.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index ended 1.92 percent lower at 491.7 and September ATX futures closed down 18 points at 1,352.0 with 3,241 contracts traded.
